cards.prompt: In Al-Waqiah 45, how are the people described as living before their punishment?
Al-Waqiah 46 says they persisted in the worst ____ (al-hinth al-azim).
cards.explanation: Their persisting in great sin is the reason described for their fate.

cards.prompt: In Al-Waqiah 47-48, what doubt did the deniers voice about death?
cards.answer: They asked whether they would really be resurrected after becoming dust and bones, and whether their forefathers would be too.

cards.prompt: According to Al-Waqiah 49-50, who will be gathered on the appointed day?
options: Only those who lived in luxury
Only the forefathers of the deniers
cards.answer: Both the earlier and later generations will be gathered for the appointed day.

cards.prompt: Al-Waqiah 49-50 answers the 'what about our forefathers?' doubt by saying that only the forefathers will be gathered.
cards.answer: Myth: the verses say all earlier and later generations will be gathered on a day that is known.

cards.prompt: A friend says 'once we turn to dust and bones, that's the end.' Which idea from Al-Waqiah 47-50 answers that?
cards.answer: The verses record this same doubt and respond that all generations, earlier and later, will certainly be gathered on an appointed day.
